chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: The Ritz Brothers flop at Loew's State and Bubbles' private vow
summary: After watching the headlining Ritz Brothers die, he vows to quit show business unless Buck and Bubbles headline the next day.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And we were picked -- the first colored act after Bert Williams. Bert Williams was the first negro that played in the Ziegfeld Follies and Buck and Bubbles was the second negros to play in the Follies. And we -- I took -- that's another job. Billy Rose for the Ziegfeld Follies. How that happened, we were playing at Loews State Theater in New York and I went to this show for the first time to see this show before we appeared. And the Ritz Brothers were playing and they were headlining the show. Ritz Brothers on the marquee,

Ritz Brothers in a banner and I wanted to catch this show and man, did they die. They died the death of a dog. So after the show I go downstairs to see the manager. So I saw the usher and told the usher to tell the manager that John Bubbles wanted to see him of Buck and Bubbles. So he says, okay, he'd go tell the manager to come out. So I could tell he was a manager because he came out in a tuxedo. He knew about Buck and Bubbles because Buck and Bubbles were going to be in his show next week. So he knew me. He wanted to know what I wanted. I said, I wanted to let you know I was here and saw that you had a wonderful show. Yeah, a rotten show. I told him it was wonderful. But I wanted to let him know I was there. I didn't want him to know that I wasn't in there to see his show and see how the headliner was flopping, had to steal a bow, and didn't give but one bow. And then I left the theater. I asked the manager what time was the rehearsal tomorrow -- he said 8 o'clock. I said, I'll

see you tomorrow, said I to he. So I leave and all the way home I'm thinking -- Ritz Brothers headlining that show. Couldn't take a bow. Imagine that. But I let the manager know I was there, didn't I? I wouldn't work in that theater any more. If we're not headlining that theater tomorrow I'm going to quit show business. That's what I'm going to do.
So I go on home and I don't sleep that night. If we don't headline that theater tomorrow, I'm going to quit show business. That's what I'm going to do.

And so I go on home and I don't sleep that night, I stay up all night that night, trying to solve how I'm going to solve how I'm going to quit the show, 'cause I'm just figuring aint going to headline it -- all night long. The next morning I get myself together to get ready to go down to rehearsal and would you believe that I go down to rehearsal and there's a jald (?) in the road at 47th Street and 7th Avenue and Broadway, there's a

jaded in the street that you get so far and you can see the theater, the front of the theater, of the Loews State Theater, the block between 43rd and 44th, and the big banner out there says "Buck and Bubbles," around the marque in lights, it says "Buck and Bubbles." This what had happened overnight. I'm saying to myself, who could have told them, -- do they care whether I quit or not. Who could have told them that I was going to quit. Nobody. Because I didn't tell a soul. My manager didn't know and my partner didn't know that it was in my mind that I was going to quit vaudeville and all the theater business. I was going to quit if the name wasn't headlined in that theater that day. And Lo and Behold --
